value: Plug in and select one of 5 heat settings (lower for fine/damaged hair, higher for coarse).
Choose rotation speed: slow while learning, fast once comfortable.
Take a small section of dry hair; open the clamp lever and place the section (ends or mid-length) against the barrel, close the clamp.
Hold the iron vertically (tip up or down) next to the head and press the directional button: the barrel rotates and wraps the section around itself.
Hold a few seconds, open the clamp and slide the iron out of the curl.
Press Home to reset the barrel before the next section; alternate direction toward/away from the face for a balanced look.
how_to_use.source: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H6CS24D5 (buttons/functions); clamp handling steps are general curling-iron practice (not stated verbatim)

grip_and_hair_interaction.value: Held in one hand like a traditional curling iron: fingers wrap the long teal handle around its middle/lower part, thumb along the inner side, barrel pointing straight up beside the head (photo 01: right hand, iron vertical at temple height). The clamp lever (dark grey thumb paddle) sits at the top of the handle where the barrel starts; directional (rocker/oval) button and round Home button are on the handle face just below the clamp collar, within thumb reach; speed/heat controls further down the handle; cord exits the bottom through a black swivel. Hair: a 3-5 cm wide section is wound in a loose spiral around the grey barrel from mid-shaft, ends tucked under the clamp near the collar; the free end of the curl drops out of the clamp area. Free hand is not needed (that is the selling point).
grip_and_hair_interaction.source: client photo 01 + https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H6CS24D5 gallery images 3-4 (button callouts)

value: Start on completely dry, detangled hair (it is not a dryer).
Choose heat: lower settings for fine/damaged hair, up to 430 F for coarse hair; press Ionic Mode on for sleek/anti-frizz or leave off for volume.
Take a section no wider than the brush; place the brush under the section at the root for lift.
Glide slowly from root to ends, letting the heated combs smooth the hair.
At mid-lengths/ends, roll the brush to wrap the hair 1-2 turns, hold a few seconds, then unroll/glide out for a bent end or soft curl.
Repeat around the head; touch up flyaways or second-day bends.
how_to_use.source: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H6GT5D2V (functions); sequence is standard thermal-brush practice

Controls (ionic button, heat buttons with small red LED dots) sit on the handle face just below the flared collar. Hair: a section from beside the face is wrapped ~1.5 turns around the middle of the bristle barrel, ends caught in the bristles; bristles hold tension. No second hand needed.

value: Start with clean, damp hair; use the Concentrator nozzle to rough-dry.
Switch to an Air Curler barrel (hold Attachment Release, twist off/on) and section hair with the creaseless clips.

Prep with mousse and heat protectant; hold the end of a section near the barrel - the Coanda airflow pulls the hair in and wraps it around the barrel; use the opposite-direction barrel on the other side of the head.
Hold until dry, lock the curl with the Cold Shot, then slide the barrel out downward.
Pin curls to cool and set, then finish with hairspray.
For blowouts use the 1 3/4" round brush (lift at root, roll through) or the paddle brush (smooth in one pass).

Style/Switch button functions (which button is power/heat/speed/cool shot/pause) are not documented in reachable sources; the user manual page was blocked.
Exact handle diameters, barrel/attachment lengths and the Style/Switch handle-only weight are estimates; a physical sample or the brand spec sheet would settle them.
Amazon weights for the Auto Curler (1.25 lb) and Thermal Round Brush (1.6 lb) disagree with the A+ copy ('just 2.2 pounds'); the A+ figure looks like shared boilerplate.
Launch dates for the Thermal Round Brush, Style/Switch BNTSSSW and Pink Rush flat iron are not shown on Amazon; only the Auto Curler has a first-available date (Sep 15 2026).
Flat iron heat chart conflict: gallery says 300/340/380/420/450 F, A+ module says 285/320/355/395/430 F; the physical LEDs on the A+ close-up read 265/300/355/390/450 F.
Hair-type matrices mix brand claims with estimates for types the brand does not show (e.g. Auto Curler on 3A-4C, Thermal Brush on 4A-4C); estimates are flagged.
